question: Carrying land units by sea: boarding, capacity, getting off, at sea, a sea battle and the fleet's end, the transport mission, save and load (WAVE.md brief A).

addresses.name: CLoadArmyCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: **Slot 6: puts a land unit aboard the fleet the command names.** Resolves `unit` (+0x3C, id at +0x40/+0x44) and `navy` (+0x64, id at +0x68/+0x6C) through FindPersistentById. Does nothing unless the unit is land (slot 15) and its CArmy +0x300 carried_by is null. Then: remembers whether the unit is selected (+4), CNavy::AddCarried(navy->AsNavy (slot 11), unit) - the call at 0x5E3B96; the `push esi` before the slot-11 call at 0x5E3B94 is AddCarried's argument -, CUnit::EnterProvince(unit, the province it is already in), the selection moved to the fleet (the in-game screen's slot 46 then Select where the unit was selected and the fleet is not; slots 45 and Select where only the fleet was), and last **the unit's order replaced by CreateOrder(0x18D) - the null order** through CUnit::SetOrder. **No province test, no port test, no cost**: nothing here or in slot 14 asks whether the unit stands where the fleet is - the posters do (the unit panel's chooser 0x75E510 walks the port's fleets), and the unit is not moved. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section A.1.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x5E3AD0-0x5E3E8C whole on the disassembly: the two FindPersistentById resolutions writing +0x3C (0x5E3B2A) and +0x64 (0x5E3B5A), slot 15 at 0x5E3B62, slot 9 then `cmp [eax+0x300], ebx; jne` at 0x5E3B79, the byte at +4 saved at 0x5E3B8D, `push esi; mov ecx,edi; call [edx+0x2C]; call 0x5CF040` at 0x5E3B91-0x5E3B96, EnterProvince(unit, [esi+0x130]) at 0x5E3BA4, the selection calls at 0x5E3C8F/0x5E3D27/0x5E3DCC/0x5E3E61, `push 0; push 0x18D; call CreateOrder` and `mov eax, esi; call SetOrder` at 0x5E3E63-0x5E3E76. Bare `ret`. vtable.py: CLoadArmyCommand slot 6 alone. Wrong if a test of the unit's or the fleet's province sat on this path - none of the reads between 0x5E3AD0 and 0x5E3E7B touches +0x130 except to pass it back to EnterProvince.

addresses.name: CLoadArmyCommand::IsValid

It asks nothing of where either stands, nor whether the unit is land or already aboard (Execute does those two and does nothing where they fail). addresses.name: CUnloadArmyCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: **Slot 6: takes a land unit off the fleet carrying it, where it stands.** Resolves `unit` (+0x3C); for a unit that resolves, RemoveFromTransport(its carried_by, carrySupplies = false, its province) with the unit in EDI, then CUnit::EnterProvince(unit, the province it is in). Nothing else - no supplies are brought from home (the byte is 0), no organisation, no order or path change. RemoveFromTransport runs CheckForCombat. The unit stands in the province it was in, which is the fleet's: a port, because slot 14 refuses anything else. Posters: 0x66A9E0 (in-game screen, 0x66A750), 0x75E458 (the unit panel's unload button, 0x75E400), 0x8D4F50 (AI, 0x8D4D40), and the AI builds one inline at 0x891FE3 (0x891BE0). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section A.3.
addresses.evidence: 0x5E3600-0x5E367E read whole: the +0x40 resolution, `mov esi,[edi+0x130]` and slot 9 then `mov ecx,[eax+0x300]`, `push esi; push 0; push ecx; call 0x5CF120` (EDI = unit), `push [edi+0x130]; mov ecx,edi; call 0x5BEFD0`, bare ret. findRefs --callers 0x5E3560 for the three poster sites, findRefs --vftable CUnloadArmyCommand for the inline one at 0x891FE3. Wrong if the byte pushed second were not 0 - it is `push 0` decoded.

The unit panel shows the refusal as UW_UNLOAD_NOT_VALID, "You can only unload if your fleet is located in a port." Nothing about the fleet's state (moving, in a battle) is asked.

addresses.name: CNavy::CanCarry
addresses.no_signature: The fleet in ECX and the land unit in EAX, bare `ret`, the answer in AL.
addresses.comment: **Whether a fleet can take a land unit aboard.** False unless: the two have one owner (+0x128); the fleet is in no battle (+0x11C <= 0), not moving (+0x140 <= 0) and not retreating (+0x158); and `unit.definition.transport_weight / 1000 + SumTransportWeight(fleet.carrying) <= fleet.definition.transport_capability / 1000`, each /1000 cut toward zero. Both figures are the units' own rebuilt definitions (CUnit +0xC8): the passenger's sum over its brigades (an ineffective support brigade adds nothing, FINDINGS-unitdef.md), the fleet's sum over every ship - only transport ships declare a capability in Their Finest Hour (transport_ship 40, invasion_transport_ship 60; an infantry_brigade weighs 10). Eight callers: CUnit::AdvanceMovement (0x5CAD03, boarding by marching onto a fleet), CArmy::MayStandIn (0x5CE2E0), CLoadArmyCommand::IsValid (0x5E4135), the unit panel's fleet chooser 0x75E510 (0x75E585), 0x653990 and 0x669AA0 (interface), and the AI at 0x8A0BD3 and 0x8D4070. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: 0x5CEFB0-0x5CF032 read whole: `mov edx,[ecx+0x128]; cmp edx,[eax+0x128]`, `cmp [ecx+0x11C],0; jg false`, `cmp [ecx+0x140],0; jg false`, `cmp byte [ecx+0x158],0; jne false`, the two magic-number /1000 on [[eax+0xC8]+0x10C] and [[ecx+0xC8]+0x144], `lea eax,[ecx+0x2E4]; call 0x5D6690`, `cmp ebx,eax; setle al; ret`. findRefs --callers 0x5CEFB0 gives the eight sites. Install units/transport.txt, tfh/units/invasion_transport_ship.txt, tfh/units/infantry_brigade.txt for the figures.

addresses.name: CNavy::AddCarried
addresses.no_signature: The fleet in EAX and the land unit on the stack, `ret 4`.
addresses.comment: **Puts a land unit on a fleet's carrying list.** Through the unit's slot 9 (AsArmy): carried_by (+0x300) = the fleet, dig_in_level (+0x1C8) = 0, staging_province (+0x2E4) = 0, and target (+0x2E8) = 0 only where the fleet is null. Returns where the unit is already listed; otherwise appends a node at the tail of the fleet's +0x2E4 list. Last, the first AI agent up the fleet's hierarchy (CUnit +0x198, then the parent's at +0x1E0) is told through its slot 69 with the CArmy. It does not touch the unit's province, path, order, movement_progress or hierarchy. Four callers: CLoadArmyCommand::Execute (0x5E3B96); CUnit::AdvanceMovement twice - a land unit marching into a sea province boards the first own fleet there that CanCarry it (0x5CAD69), and a landing that may not stand on the land after all goes back aboard (0x5CAF5F); and CNavy::LoadKey for each `division` (and the other land keys) inside a navy block (0x5CF79E). The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: 0x5CF040-0x5CF11A read whole: `mov edi,[ebp+8]; mov esi,eax`, slot 9 (+0x24) then the three stores at 0x5CF056-0x5CF062 and the conditional fourth at 0x5CF06C, the duplicate walk 0x5CF072-0x5CF08D, the 0x10-byte node {unit, prev = old tail, next 0, lock 0} at 0x5CF097-0x5CF0AE, tail/count update, the agent walk over +0x198/+0x1E0 and `call [edi+0x114]` at 0x5CF114, `ret 4`. findRefs --callers 0x5CF040 gives four sites; the CNavy::LoadKey one passes `lea eax,[ebx-8]` (0x5CF79B). CArmy +0x2E4/+0x2E8 are staging_province/target by CArmy::LoadKey's switch.

addresses.name: RemoveFromTransport
addresses.signature: void __stdcall RemoveFromTransport(CNavy* fleet@stack:4, bool carrySupplies@stack:8, CMapProvince* province@stack:0xC, CUnit* unit@EDI)
addresses.comment: **Takes one land unit off a fleet.** In order: the first AI agent up the fleet's hierarchy (+0x198, then +0x1E0's) is told through its slot 70 with (the CArmy, `province`) - the only use of `province`; carried_by (+0x300), dig_in_level (+0x1C8), staging_province (+0x2E4) and target (+0x2E8) of the CArmy zeroed; where `carrySupplies` is set, CUnit::CarrySupplies(unit, **the province the unit is in now**, false, true); the node unlinked from the fleet's list (CList_RemoveNode, which only marks it while the list is locked); CCombatManager::CheckForCombat(unit, the province it is in). It does not move the unit - every caller follows with CUnit::EnterProvince. Four callers: CUnit::EnterProvince for each passenger of a fleet ending its path in a land province (0x5BF965, carrySupplies set); CUnit::AdvanceMovement for a passenger stepping ashore (0x5CACA6, set, after clearing previous_province); CheckTransportOverload in port (0x5CFC75, clear); CUnloadArmyCommand::Execute (0x5E3666, clear). **Because the unit has not moved yet, CarrySupplies fills the pool of the province it is leaving** - for the first two callers the sea zone it was carried through.
addresses.evidence: 0x5CF120-0x5CF283 read whole: the agent walk and `push [ebp+0x10]; push AsArmy(edi); call [ebx+0x118]` at 0x5CF16A-0x5CF182; slot 9 then the four stores 0x5CF193-0x5CF1A5; `cmp byte [ebp+0xC],0; je` and `push 1; push 0; push [edi+0x130]; push edi; call 0x5BED80` at 0x5CF1AD-0x5CF1B8; the node search and `call 0x5D49D0`; `push [edi+0x130]; push edi; lea ecx,[eax+0xB5C]; call 0x430960`; `ret 0xC` at 0x5CF283. EDI is never loaded inside, so it is an argument. findRefs --callers 0x5CF120: four sites, each loading EDI with the unit first.
addresses.revises: Read whole: signature (three stack arguments and the unit in EDI), what it clears, the supplies, the AI notification, the combat check and its four callers. Was one write read and `inferred`.

addresses.name: CNavy::UnloadCarried
addresses.comment: **Puts every unit a fleet carries ashore where the fleet is**: for each node of +0x2E4, the AI agent's slot 70 with (the CArmy, the fleet's province); the CArmy's +0x300, +0x1C8, +0x2E4 and +0x2E8 zeroed; CUnit::CarrySupplies(unit, its province, false, true); the node unlinked (marked instead while the list's lock byte +0x2F0 is set); CheckForCombat(unit, its province). Unlike RemoveFromTransport it calls no EnterProvince: the units are already in the fleet's province. **One caller**, CNavalTransportOrder::IsActive at 0x5A074D, for a fleet that is in its target province and still carries something. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section A.6.

addresses.name: CheckTransportOverload
addresses.comment: **Whether a fleet carries more than it can, and what it does about it.** Overloaded where SumTransportWeight(fleet.carrying) > fleet.definition.transport_capability (+0x144) / 1000. Then, until it is not: walk the passengers in list order; one standing in a **land** province (the fleet is in port) is put ashore - RemoveFromTransport(fleet, carrySupplies = false, its province) and EnterProvince(it, its province) - and the walk goes on; at the first passenger at **sea** that still has a brigade, its first brigade is taken off (RemoveRegimentFromUnit, which rebuilds its definition) and deleted, and where that was its last brigade the unit is queued for removal (the inline CGameState::QueueUnitRemoval, CCurrentGameState +0xBF4) - then the load is measured again. Nothing tells the player. **Five callers**: CUnit::UpdateHourly for every fleet every hour (0x5BA003), CUnit::UpdateDaily behind in_game (0x5BB413), CUnitList::RemoveSpentSubUnits after each round of a battle (0x5D6653), the source fleet of a sub-unit transfer (CTransferSubUnitCommand::Execute, 0x5DCDC1) and of a split (0x5EB737, in the split helper 0x5EB620). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section A.2.
addresses.evidence: 0x5CFBD0 read whole: `add eax,0x2E4; call 0x5D6690` and `[[fleet.AsNavy]+0xC8]+0x144 / 1000` at 0x5CFBFA-0x5CFC2A; the land test `[[unit+0x130]+0xD4]+0x22` - CProvinceTemplate.is_land, settled by FINDINGS-redeploy.md - and RemoveFromTransport/EnterProvince on the set side; RemoveRegimentFromUnit on the first node of +0x38 and slot 0 delete; the {type,id} push into CCurrentGameState +0xBF4/+0xBF8's micro-queue, the same thirty instructions as CGameState::QueueUnitRemoval (0x284C80). findRefs --callers 0x5CFBD0: five sites, attributed with functionStart and checked by retsBefore (0 for all but none needing it).
addresses.revises: Which way +0x22 is (land: put ashore - in port; sea: brigades destroyed), the push is the unit-removal queue and not a message ring, it also runs every hour and after battles, splits and transfers (five callers, not the last of UpdateDaily alone), and the capacity is the `transport_capability` key.

addresses.name: CNavalTransportOrder::MayBeGiven
addresses.comment: Slot 11: the fleet (+8) in no battle, the target province (+0xC) with a naval base above level 0 (CMapProvince +0x300, its +0x20), the order's slot 8 (CNavalOrder::IsInRange) yes, and the fleet's slot 34 (CNavy::MayStandIn - owned, a port, a naval base, a controller who is a friend and no enemy) yes of the target. **It does not ask whether the fleet carries anything.** So the 'friendly land province' of ORDER_TRANSPORT_DESC is a port the fleet may lie in.
addresses.evidence: 0x5A0640-0x5A0686 read whole: `cmp [eax+0x11C],0; jle`, `mov edx,[ecx+0x300]; cmp [edx+0x20],0; jle false`, `call [eax+0x20]` (slot 8), `push [esi+0xC]; call [eax+0x88]` (slot 34), `setne al; ret`. vtable.py --holding 0x5A0640: CNavalTransportOrder slot 11 alone.

addresses.name: CNavalTransportOrder::IsActive
addresses.comment: **Slot 14, asked every hour: the whole of the transport mission.** False (the order ends) for a fleet with no base (+0x98) or where CNavalOrder::IsActive says so. True and nothing more for a fleet in a battle, or once return-to-base (+0x18) is set. Where the fleet may not stand in the target (slot 34): COrder::OrderReturnToBase unless it is at its base already. Otherwise, with the fleet not moving (+0x140 <= 0): **at its base and carrying something** - NavalOrder_GoTo(target), a safe path; **in the target and carrying something** - CNavy::UnloadCarried; **in the target and empty** - OrderReturnToBase; **anywhere else** - NavalOrder_SetPathFrom(where it is, safe) to the target. A fleet that is moving is left to move. So it waits at its base for passengers, sails, unloads, goes home; and since the fleet's entering the target at the end of its path already puts its passengers ashore (CUnit::EnterProvince), the unload here is the fallback and the usual next hour is the return. Slot 13 (Start) is the empty stub 0xABF890.
addresses.evidence: 0x5A0690-0x5A0774 read whole on the listing: `cmp [esi+0x98],0; jne` else false; `cmp [esi+0x11C],0; jg true`; call 0x59B070, `je false`; `cmp byte [ebx+0x18],0; jne true`; `call [eax+0x88]` (slot 34) with the target; the base province through [[esi+0x98]] slot 0 compared with [esi+0x130]; `cmp [esi+0x140],0; jg true`; `cmp [esi+0x2EC],0` twice; `mov ecx,[ebx+0xC]; mov eax,esi; call 0x59A700`; `push esi; call 0x5CFE10`; `push ebx; call 0x5878C0`; `push 1; push eax; call 0x59A640` with ESI = fleet and EDI = target. vtable.py --holding 0x5A0690: CNavalTransportOrder slot 14 alone.

addresses.name: CUnit_MergeInto
addresses.comment: **Merges one unit into another**: every brigade of `from` moved to `into`; where both are fleets, every land unit `from` carries moved onto `into`'s list with carried_by = `into` (dig_in_level and staging_province zeroed, as CNavy::AddCarried does) - **where `into` is not a fleet they stay on `from`'s list**; where both are air units, what `from` carries likewise (+0x304, +0x2E8 zeroed); the better leader kept; `into` rebuilt (RebuildDefinition, RebuildAvatar) and put back into its province. Nothing here checks `into`'s capacity - the next CheckTransportOverload does. Callers: CMergeCommand::Execute (0x5DBCF6), CJoinFleetOrder's slot 14 (0x59BCB1) and CJoinAirOrder's (0x597C4D), each queueing `from` for removal after. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: 0x5CDC90-0x5CDFEF: `mov ebx,[ebp+8]; mov esi,[ebp+0xC]; cmp esi,ebx; je end`, the regiment loop, the IsNaval (slot 16) tests on both and the +0x2E4 walk with slot 9 stores of +0x300/+0x1C8/+0x2E4 (and +0x2E8 only for a null fleet) at 0x5CDDE0, the IsAir (slot 17) arm through slot 13 writing +0x304/+0x2E8, RebuildDefinition/RebuildAvatar/EnterProvince at 0x5CDFC5-0x5CDFE4, `ret 8`. findRefs --callers 0x5CDC90: three sites, attributed by vtable (CMergeCommand slot 6 0x5DB9E0, CJoinFleetOrder slot 14 0x59BC40, CJoinAirOrder slot 14 0x597BB0).

addresses.name: CUnit_RelinkLoadedParent
addresses.comment: **Puts a unit loaded out of its carrier's block back under its parent.** Where the id pair a save's `parent` key left at CUnit +0x54/+0x58 is not the null id, it resolves it and attaches the unit to it (0x5B9760(unit, parent)). One caller, CInGameIdler::Enter (0x65B803), for every unit of every country's list as the game is entered. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: 0x5CEDC0-0x5CEE1C: `cmp [esi+0x58],[0x1A8CC98]` / `cmp [esi+0x54],[0x1A8CC94]` against the null id, FindPersistentById (0xA9DA00), `add eax,-8`, `push eax; push esi; call 0x5B9760`, bare ret. CArmy::LoadKey's `parent` arm writes `this+0x4C` with this = CArmy+8, i.e. +0x54; CUnit::CUnit zeroes +0x54/+0x58 at 0x5B5091. findRefs --callers 0x5CEDC0: one site, inside CInGameIdler::Enter, in a loop over country +0xBAC.

addresses.name: CNavy::SaveContents
addresses.comment: CNavy's slot 2 of its CPersistent table (at +8, so `this` here is the fleet + 8): CUnit's contents (0x5B8170), then **every unit it carries, each as a block under the key of its oob_level** (+0x1F4: 0 theatre, 1 armygroup, 2 army, 3 corps, 4 division, 5 navy, 6 air, else none) written by the unit's own Save, then `at_sea` = **the fleet's +0x2F8, the post-battle wait**, not +0x2F0. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: 0x5CFAA0-0x5CFB80: `mov edi,ecx; call 0x5B8170`, the walk from [edi+0x2DC] (fleet +0x2E4), the jump table at 0x5CFB84 on [unit+0x1F4] giving 0x465/0x466/0x250/0x467/0x468/0x251/0x440/0x18D, `lea edi,[eax+8]; call [edx+4]`, then `mov esi,[edi+0x2F0]` (fleet +0x2F8) under token 0x3FC, `ret 4`. vtable.py --holding 0x5CFAA0: CNavy slot 2, table 0x15C8750 at object offset 8. Saves: every carried division sits in its fleet's block, `at_sea=0` on all 220 and 206 fleets of two saves.

addresses.name: CArmy::SaveContents
addresses.comment: CArmy's slot 2 of its CPersistent table (at +8): CUnit's contents, then `target` (+0x2E8) where above 0, `staging_province` (+0x2E4) where above 0, and **`parent` - the parent's id pair - only where the unit has a parent and is carried, by a fleet (+0x300) or by air (+0x304)**. So `parent` is the key a carried unit, saved outside its land hierarchy, finds its way back with. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: 0x5CECD0-0x5CEDBA: `call 0x5B8170`, `mov ebx,[edi+0x2E0]; test; jle` under token 0x6A, `mov ebx,[edi+0x2DC]` under 0x3A4, `mov eax,[edi+0x1D8]` (parent, +0x1E0) and `cmp [edi+0x2F8],0 / cmp [edi+0x2FC],0` before token 0x84 with [parent+0x10]/[+0x14]; `ret 4`. vtable.py --holding: CArmy slot 2 of table 0x15BDEB8 at object offset 8. Saves: `parent=` occurs exactly 5 times in Germany1936_04_20_03.hoi3, matching its 5 carried divisions, and once in _01_07_22, matching its one.

addresses.name: CNavy::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNavy::LoadKey(CNavy* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: What a `navy` block adds over CUnit::LoadKey; **`this` is the CPersistent subobject, CNavy + 8**. `at_sea` (0x3FC) is read into this+0x2F0, which is **CNavy +0x2F8, the post-battle wait** - not +0x2F0, so it never touches the carrying list's lock byte. `base` sets the home base through CUnit::SetBase where the province has a naval base (else logs 'can not find NAVAL base'). **`army`, `theatre`, `armygroup`, `corps` and `division`** each build a CArmy (new 0x308, ctor 0x4828C0): byte +0x48 set, oob_level from the key (0x5B8C70), slot 28 with the fleet's +0x160, the fleet's owner (0x5BC460), the block read by the unit's Load; where it then has a location it goes aboard - CNavy::AddCarried(the fleet, it), which **zeroes the dig_in and staging_province just read** and keeps `target` - and into its owner's unit list (CCountry::AddUnit); without a location it is deleted. Its `parent` is restored later, by CUnit_RelinkLoadedParent as the game is entered. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-oob.md and FINDINGS-transport.md, section A.7.
addresses.evidence: 0x5CF6A0-0x5CF800 on the listing: `mov ebx,ecx`, `cmp eax,0x3FC` then `mov [ebx+0x2F0],eax` at 0x5CF6FE; the land arm 0x5CF71B: new 0x308, call 0x4828C0, `mov byte [esi+0x48],1`, 0x5B8C70, slot 28 with [ebx+0x158], 0x5BC460 with [ebx+0x11C]/[ebx+0x120], `lea ecx,[esi+8]; call [..+0xC]`, `cmp [esi+0x130],0; je delete`, `push esi; lea eax,[ebx-8]; call 0x5CF040`. That `this` is fleet + 8 is shown in the same image by CNavy::SaveContents, whose `this+0x2DC` is the carrying list (fleet +0x2E4) and whose at_sea is `this+0x2F0`.
addresses.revises: The land-unit arm traced (it was 'embarked land units is a guess, not traced'): it builds the passenger and puts it aboard through CNavy::AddCarried. And at_sea lands on the fleet's +0x2F8, the post-battle wait, because `this` is the +8 subobject.

addresses.name: CArmy::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CArmy::LoadKey(CArmy* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: `this` is the CPersistent subobject, CArmy + 8. `target` (0x6A) into CArmy +0x2E8, `staging_province` (0x3A4) into +0x2E4 - both as integers - and `parent` (0x84) as an id pair into CUnit +0x54/+0x58, which CUnit_RelinkLoadedParent resolves as the game is entered. Anything else to CUnit::LoadKey. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section A.7.
addresses.evidence: 0x5CEC40-0x5CECC1: `sub eax,0x6A; je` -> `mov [esi+0x2E0],eax`; `sub eax,0x1A; je` -> `add esi,0x4C; push esi; call 0xA7B250`; `sub eax,0x320; je` -> `mov [esi+0x2DC],eax`; default 0x5B6E90. 0x6A+0x1A = 0x84 parent, 0x84+0x320 = 0x3A4 staging_province (saveTokens.json). CSetAIParamCommand::LoadKey maps the same two tokens to its +0x64 and +0x68, and its Execute writes CArmy +0x2E8 from +0x64 and +0x2E4 from +0x68 - the same pairing.
addresses.revises: Where each of the three keys lands, which settles CArmy +0x2E4 as staging_province and +0x2E8 as target.

struct_fields.name: staging_province
struct_fields.comment: The province id the AI stages the unit in, saved as `staging_province` (CArmy::SaveContents writes it where above 0; CArmy::LoadKey reads it). CSetAIParamCommand::Execute (0x1E9160) writes it from the command's +0x68, which its LoadKey fills from `staging_province`; CAIUnit slot 78 zeroes it at 0x4B2498. **Zeroed whenever the unit goes aboard a fleet (CNavy::AddCarried, CUnit_MergeInto) and when it leaves one (RemoveFromTransport, CNavy::UnloadCarried, CGameState::RemoveUnit)** - which is why no carried division in a save has one.
struct_fields.evidence: CArmy::LoadKey 0x5CEC40: token 0x3A4 -> [this+0x2DC] with this = CArmy+8; CArmy::SaveContents 0x5CED2F reads [edi+0x2DC] for token 0x3A4; CSetAIParamCommand::LoadKey 0x5E9343: 0x3A4 -> +0x68. Wrong if `this` in those two were not CArmy+8 - CArmy's CPersistent table sits at object offset 8 (vtable.py).
struct_fields.revises: Name ai_param_b -> staging_province, from the save key both CArmy's save and load and CSetAIParamCommand's load attach to it.

struct_fields.name: target
struct_fields.comment: The province id the AI means the unit for, saved as `target` (written where above 0). CSetAIParamCommand::Execute writes it from its +0x64 (`target`). **Kept when the unit boards a fleet** - CNavy::AddCarried zeroes it only for a null fleet - so a carried division's `target` in a save is its transport's destination (the Division de Tonkin's 6610, the 19th Indian's 6622); **zeroed when it is put ashore** (RemoveFromTransport, CNavy::UnloadCarried) and when it boards or leaves an air transport.
struct_fields.evidence: CArmy::LoadKey: token 0x6A -> [this+0x2E0] (CArmy+0x2E8); CArmy::SaveContents 0x5CECEA; CSetAIParamCommand::LoadKey 0x5E9337: 0x6A -> +0x64; CNavy::AddCarried's conditional store at 0x5CF06C. Savegames _01_07_22 to _01_08_07 and _04_20_03 for the two figures.
struct_fields.revises: Name ai_param_a -> target, from the save key.

struct_fields.name: carried_by
struct_fields.comment: The fleet carrying the army, or null. **Written** by CNavy::AddCarried (0x5CF056) and CUnit_MergeInto (0x5CDDE0); **cleared** by RemoveFromTransport (0x5CF193), CNavy::UnloadCarried (0x5CFEA1) and CGameState::RemoveUnit (0x68576B, 0x685881). Every write goes with dig_in_level (+0x1C8) = 0 and staging_province (+0x2E4) = 0; a clear with target (+0x2E8) = 0 too. Read, among others, by CUnit::RegainOrganisation (no regain at sea), CSubUnit::CanReinforce (no reinforcement), CUnit::UpdateDaily (no digging in), CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel (draws on the carrier's base), CUnit::CanEngage and CUnitList::AllHostileTo (a carried unit going nowhere fights no one), CCombatManager::CheckForCombat (nothing at all while the carrier is moving; takes no province), CUnit::CanMoveTo (no supply test before stepping onto enemy ground), CArmy::SaveContents (`parent`) and CProvinceTemplate_AddUnitCounter. ProvinceTooltip_Build gives UTM_LACK_OF_SUPPLIES only where it is null. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldchain.py --field 0x300 filtered to sites whose previous instructions call slot 9 (+0x24): 78 sites in 46 functions (six more sites the decode could not reach from their function start), the ones named read on the listing; the writers are the seven stores listed. A CMapProvince +0x300 (naval_base) read is the other big family and none of the listed sites is one.
struct_fields.revises: Comment: every writer and the readers that decide what a carried unit does, in place of the two clearers.

struct_fields.name: loaded_parent
struct_fields.comment: The id half of the parent a save's `parent` key named (the type half at +0x58), read by CArmy::LoadKey; CUnit::CUnit zeroes both (0x5B5091). CUnit_RelinkLoadedParent (0x1CEDC0) resolves it as the game is entered and attaches the unit. Only a carried unit is saved with `parent`.
struct_fields.evidence: CArmy::LoadKey: `add esi,0x4C; push esi; push parse; call 0xA7B250` with esi = CArmy+8; CUnit_RelinkLoadedParent compares [unit+0x54]/[unit+0x58] with the null id 0x1A8CC94/0x1A8CC98; CUnit::CUnit `mov [edi+0x54],ebx; mov [edi+0x58],ebx`.

struct_fields.name: carrying_no_unlink
struct_fields.comment: The fourth member of the `carrying` list at +0x2E4 - CList's deferred-deletion lock: CNavy::UnloadCarried tests it (0x5CFEE2) and marks the node instead of unlinking while it is set. CNavy::CNavy zeroes it with a byte store (0x5CEE4B). **It is not `at_sea`**: CNavy::LoadKey's and CNavy::SaveContents's `this` is the fleet + 8, so the `at_sea` key is the fleet's +0x2F8 (the post-battle wait). The collision CANDIDATES.md proposed a live check for does not exist.
struct_fields.evidence: CNavy::SaveContents 0x5CFAA0 walks the passengers from [this+0x2DC] - the carrying list, fleet +0x2E4 - and writes at_sea from [this+0x2F0]; the same `this` therefore puts at_sea at fleet +0x2F8. CNavy::LoadKey's write at 0x5CF6FE is `[ebx+0x2F0]` with ebx = that `this`. CNavy::CNavy at 0x5CEE4B: `mov byte ptr [esi+0x2F0], al`.
struct_fields.revises: Name at_sea -> carrying_no_unlink and type int -> uint8_t: the at_sea key lands eight bytes higher, on +0x2F8.

struct_fields.name: combat_cooldown
struct_fields.comment: **A fleet's post-combat cooldown, in hours** (slot-31 ticks). ShouldStartNavalCombat refuses to start a combat while it is above zero (0x31889, via AsNavy()). Set to `8 + (rand() % 8)` when the fleet leaves a battle, decremented by CNavy::CheckOrderAndCombat, zeroed by CUnit::EnterProvince when the fleet enters another province. **Saved and loaded as `at_sea`** (CNavy::SaveContents, CNavy::LoadKey - both with `this` = fleet + 8, the offset 0x2F0 they use being this one).
struct_fields.evidence: CNavy::SaveContents 0x5CFB33 `mov esi,[edi+0x2F0]` under token 0x3FC with edi = fleet+8; CNavy::LoadKey 0x5CF6FE; the two saves' at_sea=0 on every fleet agree with a wait that is nought outside the hours after a battle.
struct_fields.revises: Comment: it is the field saved as `at_sea`, and EnterProvince's zeroing.

struct_fields.name: transport_capability
struct_fields.comment: The `transport_capability` key: how much a ship (or a transport plane) carries, in thousandths of transport_weight. Summed over a unit's ships by RebuildDefinition. transport_ship 40, invasion_transport_ship 60 in Their Finest Hour; every other ship declares 0. CNavy::CanCarry and CheckTransportOverload compare it /1000 with the summed weights /1000.
struct_fields.evidence: CSubUnitDefinition::LoadKey 0x5A3C80: `cmp eax,0x48D; ... je 0x5A43D1` and at 0x5A43EA `mov [edi+0x144],eax`; saveTokens.json 0x48D = transport_capability, and no token transport_capacity exists. The unit files use transport_capability and never transport_capacity.
struct_fields.revises: Name transport_capacity -> transport_capability, the key the loader reads into it.

slots_noted: CUnit slots 9, 11 and 13 are the downcasts: the folded ReturnThis (0x5B4EC0) in CArmy's, CNavy's and CAir's own table respectively and the folded zero 0xA80690 elsewhere; slots 10, 12 and 14 hold the same pairs and are left unnamed. CUnloadArmyCommand's slots 2 and 4 are bodies eight unit commands share (0x5E3330 save, 0x5E3380 CDisbandCommand::LoadKey) and are left as they are.
